concept: Free fall with quadratic air drag (drag grows with speed squared) leads to an asymptotic speed limit.

misconceptions.label: Speed keeps increasing forever
misconceptions.why_tempting: Without air, 10 s of falling would mean 98 m/s.
misconceptions.refutation: Drag grows with speed until it balances gravity, so speed levels off below 50 m/s.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified

misconceptions.label: Already at top speed
misconceptions.why_tempting: Top speed sounds like something you hit and stay at.
misconceptions.refutation: It only approaches 50 m/s and never quite gets there: after 10 s it's at about 48 m/s.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified

misconceptions.label: Drag holds it back early
misconceptions.why_tempting: Air resistance feels like it acts from the start.
misconceptions.refutation: At low speed drag is tiny, so the object first speeds up at nearly g.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified

items.prompt: A falling object's top speed in air is 50 m/s (quadratic air drag). Dropped from rest, about how fast is it going after 10 seconds?

extremes.watch: Lighter objects hit their low terminal velocity very quickly.
Objects with high terminal velocity accelerate longer before leveling off.
